title_prefix: tx messages are fully validated, admitte
mechanism: handle-tx (src/networking/protocol.lisp:1816-1953) has the RejectIncomingTxs equivalent but no initial-block-download-p gate anywhere. Core's TX branch of ProcessMessage returns immediately while IsInitialBlockDownload() is true, after RejectIncomingTxs and BEFORE deserialising the transaction (refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:4479-4483, 'Stop processing the transaction early if we are still in IBD since we don't have enough information to validate it yet'), with no punishment. The inv half of the same gate IS implemented on our side (src/networking/protocol.lisp:812-816 gates AddTxAnnouncement on (not (initial-block-download-p chain-state))), so the two halves of one Core rule disagree. The path is live in production: dispatch-ibd-message (src/networking/ibd.lisp:1611) routes every command other than block/headers to handle-message, and the IBD pump's node-context carries :mempool and :peers (src/networking/ibd.lisp:3202-3207).
consequence: Throughout the IBD window any peer can make us run full mempool validation against a UTXO view that is at a stale height, admit the result to the mempool, and announce it onward. Three distinct damages, all executed: (a) wrong accept and relay -- a transaction validated against our stale coins view enters the mempool and is queued for announcement to another peer, which is exactly the judgement Core refuses to make; (b) wrong reject with persistence -- a transaction that is final at the network tip but not at our stale height is rejected and cached in the MAIN rejects filter, which is not cleared when IBD ends, so we refuse to re-download it afterwards; (c) amplification -- during IBD almost every relayed transaction spends outputs we have not synced, so each one becomes an orphanage entry plus a getdata burst for its parents plus tracker entries, competing with block download for the same bandwidth and the same sync thread. S2 rather than S3 because (a) is a wrong accept and (b) is a cached wrong reject that outlives IBD; S2 rather than S1 because the orphanage and the tracker are individually capped.
evidence: All probes driven through the shipped IBD dispatcher bl.net::dispatch-ibd-message. (1) ga11-p2-ibd, *cached-is-ibd* bound to T: (:IBD-P T :IN-MEMPOOL T :QUEUED-FOR-RELAY 1 :INV-ANNOUNCEMENT-TRACKED 0) -- the tx was validated, admitted and queued for relay to a second peer, while an inv for the same wtxid in the same pass was correctly refused (0 announcements tracked), which is the built-in positive control that the IBD predicate really reported T. (2) ga11-p2-orphan-amplification, 50 unsolicited txs spending unsynced outputs: (:TXS-SENT 50 :ORPHANS-HELD 49 :GETDATA-MESSAGES-EMITTED 49 :PARENT-ANNOUNCEMENTS-TRACKED 49 :TX-RATE-BUCKET (10.0 . 50.0)). (3) ga11-p2-stale-height-poisons-rejects, a tx with nLockTime 500 at our stale height 200: (:OUR-HEIGHT 200 :IBD-P T :IN-MEMPOOL NIL :WTXID-IN-MAIN-REJECTS T :WTXID-IN-RECONSIDERABLE NIL) -- the main rejects filter, not the reconsiderable one. Ours: src/networking/protocol.lisp:1816-1953, :812-816 (the inv gate), :668-695 (initial-block-download-p); src/networking/ibd.lisp:1611, :1716-1719, :3202-3207. Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:4479-4483.
fix_shape: Put Core's gate in the same place Core does: in handle-tx, immediately after the ignore-incoming-txs-p / peer-relays-txs-p disconnect check and before bl.ser:parse-tx-payload, return NIL when (initial-block-download-p chain-state) -- no logging of a reject reason, no rejects cache entry, no orphan intake, no misbehaviour, matching net_processing.cpp:4479-4483. Reuse the predicate the inv handler already calls at protocol.lisp:812-816 so the two halves cannot drift again, and pin the pairing with a test that drives both a tx and an inv through dispatch-ibd-message under *cached-is-ibd* and asserts neither the mempool, the orphanage, the rejects filters nor the tx-request tracker changed. Nothing else moves: the IBD predicate already latches exactly once, and the gate must not extend to the block or headers arms of the dispatcher.
